Theme

# Philosophy quotes about power

Power is the capacity to affect others and to shape what counts as possible—central to politics and ethics.

28 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

## Why this theme matters

Philosophers analyze domination, authority, freedom, and the micro-politics of everyday life. Power can enable justice or crush it.

## In the history of philosophy

From classical statecraft and Legalism to modern liberalism, Marxism, and Foucaultian analysis, the theme links institutions to the soul.

## Thinkers in this collection

[Francis Bacon](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/francis-bacon) , [Han Feizi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/han-feizi) , [Thomas Hobbes](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/thomas-hobbes) , [John Stuart Mill](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-stuart-mill) , [Dhammapada](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/dhammapada) , [Thomas Aquinas](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/thomas-aquinas) , [John Locke](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/john-locke) , [Wang Fuzhi](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/wang-fuzhi)

## Frequently asked questions

### What is power in philosophy?

It is the ability to produce effects—especially over people—through force, authority, ideology, or structure.

### Is power always bad?

No. Many theories distinguish empowering capacity from domination, and ask how power can be accountable.
